claim: Cross-domain transfer failure cannot be resolved by standard neural regularization
paper_safe_wording: Conventional regularization (label smoothing 0.05, feature noise 10%) degraded target ROC-AUC by -5.8% to -15.3% relative to the baseline (0.6075).

claim: Reported A1 PR-AUC = 0.5597 is a trapezoidal integration artifact
paper_safe_wording: Under standard Average Precision, A1 achieved AP = 0.2575 (below baseline A0 AP = 0.2978). The previously reported trapezoidal value of 0.5597 was inflated by linear interpolation across a non-differentiating probability ceiling.

claim: Feature noise collapses ranking capability to near random chance
paper_safe_wording: Injecting 10% input feature noise during training caused target-domain ranking to collapse near chance (ROC-AUC 0.514–0.516).

claim: Target calibration fails to achieve acceptable operational FPR
paper_safe_wording: Target-calibrated thresholds yielded prohibitive false positive rates (77.25% to 96.68%), rendering unadapted models operationally unviable.

claim: Neural regularization widens the source-to-target generalization gap
paper_safe_wording: All regularized models exhibited larger generalization gaps (2.3567–2.5356) than the baseline (2.2078), confirming that source-domain optimization does not resolve target distribution mismatch.
